items.headline: OpenAI will let outside groups safety-test models during training
items.summary: OpenAI announced it will allow independent evaluators, including METR and Redwood Research, to assess its models' "safety cases" and safeguard resilience earlier in the development pipeline rather than only after training completes. The move follows scrutiny of OpenAI's internal safety practices and mirrors similar third-party evaluation commitments recently made by Anthropic.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, cutting API prices by half
items.summary: OpenAI released gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna in its API, ChatGPT and Codex, claiming the new models cut factual-error rates roughly in half versus their predecessors while costing 50% less than the prior 5.6-series models. Sol targets complex coding and agentic workflows, intensifying price competition among frontier model providers.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.7, its most capable coding model yet
items.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.7, trained with a longer reinforcement-learning run on harder, longer-horizon tasks, posting notable gains on coding benchmarks like CursorBench 4.0 and DeepSWE v1.1 over Grok 4.6. The model is rolling out in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and the Grok API at unchanged pricing.

items.headline: MIT's AI-controlled microrobot gets 450% faster, does insect-like somersaults
items.summary: MIT researchers built a new AI flight controller for their coin-sized flapping-wing microrobot, boosting its speed by about 450% and letting it complete 10 consecutive somersaults in 11 seconds while resisting strong wind gusts. The advance could bring tiny robots closer to practical use in search-and-rescue and confined-space inspection.

items.headline: AI helps mathematicians crack decades-old inverse Galois problem
items.summary: Combining human insight with AI-assisted search, mathematicians resolved roughly 25,000 open cases of an inverse Galois problem concerning which symmetry groups arise from polynomial equations of degree 24 — a challenge posed by 19th-century mathematician Évariste Galois. The project illustrates how AI can expand the scale of problems considered computationally tractable in pure mathematics.

items.headline: Major banks warn AI shopping agents are outpacing fraud protections
items.summary: A coalition including Bank of America, NatWest, ING, Capital One and Commonwealth Bank of Australia warned regulators that AI shopping agents from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are being adopted faster than safeguards can keep up, citing scam, fraud and data-privacy risks. The group is pushing for rules requiring disclosure when an AI agent handles a transaction and stronger protection of payment data.

items.headline: Altman and Amodei to brief UN Security Council on AI risks
items.summary: OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei are expected to address a French-convened UN Security Council session on AI and international security, alongside Yoshua Bengio, Hugging Face's Clément Delangue, and representatives from China's DeepSeek and Moonshot. The high-profile briefing reflects growing international concern over frontier AI's geopolitical and security implications.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches new institute to widen AGI debate
items.summary: Google DeepMind launched the DeepMind Institute, led by co-founder Shane Legg and chaired by Demis Hassabis, aiming to surface a broader range of perspectives on artificial general intelligence from inside and outside the company. It's Hassabis's first major public initiative since stepping back from DeepMind's CEO role into a chairman position following the unit's recent reorganization.

items.headline: Nvidia's Rubin AI platform enters full production
items.summary: Nvidia confirmed its next-generation Rubin AI computing platform, comprising six new chips, is now in full production, with cloud partners including AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft and CoreWeave set to deploy Rubin-based instances later this year. Frontier labs such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and xAI are counted among early adopters looking to Rubin to train larger models.

items.headline: Humanoid robots post record sprint and jump marks as industry pivots to factory work
items.summary: China's Tiangong Ultra clocked a 100-meter sprint of roughly 8.6-8.9 seconds and cleared high-jump marks near 2.9-3.4 meters at recent competitive showcases, underscoring rapid locomotion progress in humanoid robotics. Meanwhile, manufacturers like UBTech and AgiBot are shifting emphasis from demonstrations toward real-world factory and logistics deployments as Unitree's public listing draws fresh capital into the sector.

items.headline: CorTec brain-computer interface earns second FDA Breakthrough Device tag
items.summary: CorTec's Brain Interchange implant received a second US FDA Breakthrough Device Designation, this time covering its use to restore communication for people with severe disabilities. The designation accelerates the regulatory review pathway for a device that links neural signals to external communication systems.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol reaches 'Astra-level' reliability at a fraction of the cost
items.summary: OpenAI said internal factuality evaluations based on real-world flagged conversations show GPT-6 Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its 5.6-series predecessor, approaching the reliability of its larger Astra model while priced at roughly $2/$10 per million input/output tokens. The release underscores an industry-wide push to close the gap between cheaper and flagship-tier models.
